clue.text: A dumb show rejected by Job's first girl?

indicators.note: first asks for the opening letter of the word Job's
rejected means thrown back, so the phrase a dumb show is read backwards

parts.note: a dumb show is a mime, acting without words

explanation.surface: A riddle about which girl a silent performance was turned down by.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rejected' turns A MIME into EMIMA. In the Book of Job, Jemima is the first of Job's three daughters born after his trials, hence the question mark.
explanation.definitionFit: A girl's name, and fittingly the name of the first daughter of Job in the Bible.

clue.text: Judge with loss of memory dropping name of a novelist

indicators.note: dropping means the letter for name falls to the bottom of this down entry

parts.note: amnesia is loss of memory

explanation.surface: A forgetful judge who cannot recall a writer's name.
explanation.walkthrough: 'dropping' moves the N of AMNESIA down to the end, giving AMESIAN.
explanation.definitionFit: Jamesian describes things relating to Henry James, the American-born novelist.

clue.text: People may be caught by this slogan frequently uttered quietly

definitions.text: People may be caught by this

parts.note: a mantra is a phrase repeated often, as in meditation
P stands for piano, the musical direction for quiet

explanation.surface: A catchphrase whispered over and over that could trap people.
explanation.definitionFit: A mantrap is a trap set for trespassers, so people are caught in it.

clue.text: Tide's beginning to stop mermaids swimming in current location

indicators.note: to stop means to plug a gap, so one letter goes inside the jumble
swimming means moving about, so the letters of mermaids are rearranged
beginning asks for the first letter of the word Tide's

explanation.surface: The tide starting to halt mermaids swimming where they are in the water.
explanation.walkthrough: 'swimming' rearranges MERMAIDS and 'to stop' puts T into that jumble. 'current' looks like present, but it is a stream's flow.
explanation.definitionFit: The middle of a stream is a place within its current, flowing water.

clue.text: Small sack for waste

parts.note: S is the usual abbreviation for small, as on clothing labels
to sack a town is to plunder it, so sack means pillage

explanation.surface: A tiny bag meant for rubbish.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sack' looks like a bag but is plunder.
explanation.definitionFit: Spilt liquid or material is lost and wasted, so spillage is waste.

clue.text: Picnicker, I hear, chewed grouse

indicators.note: chewed means mangled, so the letters of the three words are mixed up

explanation.surface: A picnicker is said to have chewed on a game bird.
explanation.walkthrough: 'I hear' looks like a sound signal, but it is fodder; 'grouse' looks like a complaint.
explanation.definitionFit: The prairie chicken is a North American grouse of open grassland.

clue.text: Minimal rent — about a shilling

indicators.note: about means around, so the word for rent goes round the other letters

parts.note: to let a property is to rent it out
S is the abbreviation for the old British shilling coin, from Latin solidus

explanation.surface: The smallest rent, around a shilling.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rent' looks like a payment, but it is the verb, LET.
explanation.definitionFit: Least means smallest in amount, the bare minimum.

clue.text: Having high hopes without good drug

indicators.note: without means the letter for good is left out

parts.note: aspiring means having ambitions or hopes

explanation.surface: An ambitious person going without a beneficial medicine.
explanation.definitionFit: Aspirin is a common painkilling drug, acetylsalicylic acid.

clue.text: Retriever not following one who uses acid

indicators.note: not means the letter for following is taken away

parts.note: a retriever is a dog that fetches, so a fetcher
F is the abbreviation for following, as in pages ff

explanation.surface: A gun dog lagging behind someone who takes acid.
explanation.walkthrough: 'one who uses acid' suggests drugs, but an etcher bites designs into metal with acid.
explanation.definitionFit: An etcher engraves plates by letting acid eat away the exposed metal.

clue.text: Little girl and boy penning poem with Australian can produce set piece

indicators.note: penning means enclosing, so the girl and boy hold the poem between them

parts.note: Cath is a short form of the girl's name Catherine
Ray is a boy's name
an ode is a lyric poem
tube is Australian slang for a can of beer

explanation.surface: A girl and boy writing verse with an Australian can create a staged item.
explanation.walkthrough: 'set piece' looks like a planned move, but it is a component of a television set.
explanation.definitionFit: The cathode-ray tube was the picture tube at the heart of an old television set.

clue.text: Rondo capriciously included by old lady in singular performance

indicators.note: included by means the jumbled letters sit inside the word for old lady

parts.note: old lady is slang for mother, here MAMA

indicators.note: capriciously means on a whim, so the letters of rondo are rearranged at random

explanation.surface: A rondo played on a whim within a one-person show by an elderly woman.
explanation.walkthrough: 'old lady' is MAMA, the longer form of mother, not the usual MA; 'singular' points to one performer, not a grammatical number.
explanation.definitionFit: A monodrama is a dramatic piece for a single performer, a solo show.

clue.text: Harsh prince taking every second jelly

indicators.note: taking every second means using only the even-placed letters of the words harsh prince

explanation.surface: A severe prince grabs every other jelly at the feast.
explanation.definitionFit: Aspic is a savoury jelly made from meat stock, used to set cold dishes.

clue.text: Improvised score

definitions.meaning: made up quickly from whatever is at hand
to score a surface is to mark it with a line or groove

explanation.definitionFit: A scratch team is improvised, and to scratch a surface is to score it.

clue.text: One no longer working on Scottish island

parts.note: RE means on or about, as in business letters
Tiree is an island of the Inner Hebrides off western Scotland

explanation.surface: Someone who has stopped working and lives on a Hebridean island.
explanation.definitionFit: A pensioner who has left employment for good is no longer working.

clue.text: Liberal with no former partner for instance

indicators.note: with no means the former partner is taken away from the longer word

parts.note: for instance is a way of introducing an example
an ex is a former husband, wife or partner

explanation.surface: A member of the Liberal party who, for instance, has no ex.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Liberal' with its capital looks political, but here it means generous.
explanation.definitionFit: Liberal in its sense of generous or plentiful matches ample, more than enough.

clue.text: By the grace of God grabbing favourably placed house

indicators.note: grabbing means the abbreviation holds the next phrase inside it

parts.note: DG stands for Dei gratia, Latin for by the grace of God, printed on British coins
well in means favourably placed, in a good position

explanation.surface: A house in a good spot, thanks to divine favour.
explanation.definitionFit: A dwelling is a house or any place where someone lives.

clue.text: Red Army withdrawal that put back All Fools' Day?

definitions.meaning: the 1934-35 retreat of China's Communist army under Mao

definitions.text: that put back All Fools' Day?
definitions.meaning: a whimsical month extended so the first of April comes later

explanation.definitionFit: The Long March was the Chinese Communist retreat; a longer third month would delay April 1st.

clue.text: Having excellent vision, join team for audition

indicators.note: for audition means the words are to be heard, so their sound is what counts

parts.note: join means link and team means side

explanation.surface: Someone sharp-sighted joining a team at a tryout.
explanation.walkthrough: 'audition' looks like a tryout, but it means hearing: LINK SIDE said aloud.
explanation.definitionFit: The lynx is famed for keen sight, so lynx-eyed means sharp-sighted.

clue.text: Tree bearing final bits of foliage rises from soil

indicators.note: bearing means carrying, so the tree holds the picked letters inside it

parts.note: the birch is a tree with pale bark

indicators.note: final bits of asks for the last letter of each of the words foliage rises from

explanation.surface: A tree carrying the last of its leaves grows up out of the earth.
explanation.walkthrough: 'final bits of' gives E, S and M, which sit after the B of BIRCH. 'soil' looks like a noun, but it is the verb, to dirty.
explanation.definitionFit: To besmirch is to stain or dirty, literally or a reputation, as to soil does.

clue.text: Doctor even cut swathe

indicators.note: to doctor is to tamper with, so the letters of even are altered

parts.note: to lop is to cut off

explanation.surface: A doctor even trims a bandage.
explanation.walkthrough: 'swathe' looks like a strip, but it is the verb, to wrap.
explanation.definitionFit: To swathe something is to wrap it up completely, to envelop it.

clue.text: Disagreeable onset of nettle rash in East End

indicators.note: onset of asks for the first letter of nettle
in London's East End the Cockney accent drops the opening H of words

parts.note: rash means hasty, acting without thought

explanation.surface: An unpleasant nettle rash starting up in east London.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rash' looks like a skin complaint but is hasty. The Cockney speech of London's East End drops an initial H, so HASTY becomes ASTY.
explanation.definitionFit: Nasty and disagreeable are synonyms for unpleasant or offensive.

clue.text: Leaders in South Atlantic letting dog jump on ice

indicators.note: leaders in asks for the first letters of the words South Atlantic letting

parts.note: a chow is a Chinese breed of dog

explanation.surface: In the South Atlantic a dog is allowed to leap on the ice.
explanation.definitionFit: A salchow is a figure-skating jump, named after the skater Ulrich Salchow.

clue.text: Dexterous cricketer's last to get into trouble over appeal

indicators.note: over means placed above, in a down entry before the next piece
to get into means the letter enters the word for trouble

parts.note: ado means fuss or trouble

indicators.note: last asks for the final letter of cricketer's

parts.note: it means sex appeal, as in the it girl

explanation.surface: A skilful cricketer finally gets in trouble over an appeal to the umpire.
explanation.walkthrough: 'appeal' suggests the cricket shout, but it is IT, sex appeal; 'over' is not a cricket over.
explanation.definitionFit: Adroit and dexterous both mean skilful with the hands or mind.

clue.text: Showing no emotion about depravity and wicked behaviour

indicators.note: about means around, so the first word wraps the second

parts.note: dry humour shows no emotion, being deadpan
depravity is moral evil

explanation.surface: A deadpan account of corruption and bad conduct.
explanation.definitionFit: Devilry is mischief or wickedness, behaviour fit for a devil.

clue.text: Daily changes where Croesus was king

indicators.note: changes means the letters of daily are rearranged

explanation.surface: A newspaper alters its coverage of an ancient wealthy king.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Daily' is a newspaper in the surface, but just fodder here.
explanation.definitionFit: Croesus, famed for his wealth, ruled the ancient kingdom in western Asia Minor.

clue.text: Group of buildings with real and imaginary parts

definitions.meaning: a set of related buildings, such as a sports or shopping centre
in mathematics a number with both a real and an imaginary part

explanation.definitionFit: A complex is a cluster of buildings, and a complex number has real and imaginary parts.

clue.text: Abandoned lodge regarded with desire

indicators.note: abandoned means wild or unrestrained, so the letters of lodge are let loose

explanation.surface: A deserted cottage was looked at longingly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Abandoned' reads as deserted, but it means unrestrained, the anagram signal.
explanation.definitionFit: To ogle is to stare at someone with obvious desire.

clue.text: Find lady taking no notice? That's weird

parts.note: to unearth is to dig up or discover

indicators.note: taking no means the notice is removed from the word lady

parts.note: an ad is a notice, an advertisement

explanation.surface: A woman discovered ignoring all notices: how strange.
explanation.walkthrough: 'notice' looks like attention, but it is an advert, AD.
explanation.definitionFit: Unearthly means not of this world, so eerie or weird.

clue.text: Murphy seizing power with a cheap drink

indicators.note: seizing means holding, so the potato word takes the next letters inside it

parts.note: murphy and tater are both slang words for a potato
P is the symbol for power in physics

explanation.surface: Someone called Murphy grabbing power along with an inexpensive beverage.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Murphy' looks like an Irish surname, but it is slang for a potato.
explanation.definitionFit: Water from the mains costs next to nothing compared with bottled drinks.

clue.text: Cast including Orson Welles initially presented

indicators.note: including means the word for cast holds the picked letters inside

parts.note: to cast off something, like a skin, is to shed it

indicators.note: initially asks for the first letters of Orson and Welles

explanation.surface: A film cast featuring Orson Welles was put on show.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cast' looks like a film's actors but is the verb, shed.
explanation.definitionFit: To have shown something is to have presented it to view.
